title: Prune and stabilize GPU dependency paths with modular micro-bundles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need to eliminate long-standing instability and slow cold-starts caused by a monolithic GPU runtime that pulls large CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS footprints at startup. This ticket implements a modular micro-bundle approach: split the runtime into minimal core + opt-in kernel bundles (quant, int8, fused-gemm variants), add a deterministic manifest generator, and introduce a small compatibility shim that chooses the appropriate CUTLASS dispatch at runtime.

Goals:
- Reduce runtime probe/startup jitter by 30-60% in mixed-tenant environments.
- Make kernel selection deterministic and auditable across CUDA 12/13 and Triton 2/3.
- Shrink base image footprint to speed container cold starts and reduce OOMs during init.
- Provide safe fallback and rollback paths when newer kernel bundles fail.

Approach:
1) Split: create micro-bundles for: common-core (minimal runtime), cutlass-core, cutlass-legacy, triton-adapter, quant-kernels. Each bundle is a small tarball with a manifest and signature.
2) Manifest: deterministic manifest builder at packaging time that enumerates symbols, ABI fingerprint, supported CUDA/Triton combinations, and a SHA256 artifact id.
3) Loader: lightweight loader inside runtime to resolve bundles by manifest matching, with a 200ms probe timebox. If matching fails, fall back to signed legacy bundle.
4) Shim: implement a thin CUTLASS dispatch shim that can route to multiple implementations without global symbol collisions (local namespace isolation).
5) CI & Testing: add matrixed CI for CUDA12/CUDA13 x Triton2/Triton3 x quant/non-quant. Add perf microbenchmarks to assert < 2% P99 increase vs current baseline for steady-state inference.
6) Telemetry & Safety: runtime emits bundle selection telemetry and probe timing. Canary rollout: start with internal reserved fleet, then 10% prod traffic, then ramp.

Trade-offs considered:
- Packaging micro-bundles increases release artifact count and slightly complicates delivery; accepted because it materially reduces runtime coupling and makes rollbacks targeted.
- A 200ms probe timebox might be too aggressive for some older hardware; we will gate that with feature flags and a per-node probe cache.

Acceptance criteria:
- Build pipeline produces signed micro-bundles with manifest and verification step.
- Startup median latency reduced by >=30% on a representative mixed-tenant cluster (internal perf run).
- Probe timebox enforced and documented; fallback path validated in CI.
- End-to-end canary deployment executed with rollback plan completed and documented.
- Regression tests (functional + perf) in CI passing for CUDA12/13 and Triton2/3 matrix.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect symbol isolation could create hard-to-debug crashes. Mitigate by unit tests that validate symbol namespaces and by running stress canaries for 48h before wider rollout.
- New packaging pipeline could break existing deploy tooling; mitigation: keep legacy bundle builder as opt-in until canary is green.

Deliverables:
- Runtime micro-bundle packaging tool (packager).
- Deterministic manifest spec and generator.
- Loader + shim implementation in runtime.
- CI matrix + perf benchmarks + canary playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Signed micro-bundles are produced in CI with manifest and SHA256 verified
Startup median latency reduced by >=30% in internal mixed-tenant benchmark
Probe timebox (200ms) enforced; fallback path triggers and is validated in >95% of simulated mismatch cases
CI matrix shows no functional regressions across CUDA12/CUDA13 and Triton2/Triton3
Canary rollout executed on internal fleet -> 10% prod -> 50% with documented rollback checklist
